title: Add jurisdictional KMS routing and compact audit rehydration for installer
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Adds installer-level jurisdictional KMS routing support and a compact audit rehydration pipeline for air-gapped and low-bandwidth deployments. Backwards-compatible runtime flags and migration steps for existing private installs.
description:
Motivation: Customers deploying Redwood Private in regulated environments requested installer-first enforcement for region-bound key usage and a lightweight audit replay path for constrained networks (air-gapped customer sites and field appliances). This PR adds jurisdictional KMS routing hooks to the private-installer control plane, an installer preflight that validates customer KMS profiles against allowed geozones, and a compact audit envelope rehydration tool to restore full audit entries from compressed traces for post-incident compliance reviews.

What this change does (high level): adds a KMS routing module to the installer that: 1) validates CMK scope annotations provided in the installation manifest; 2) compiles a jurisdictional routing table and injects a per-node KMS proxy configuration; 3) surfaces a preflight failure when a provided KMS key is incompatible with the selected data residency policy. Adds an audit rehydration utility (audit-rehydrate) packaged with the installer that consumes compact audit envelopes produced by the runtime and reconstructs canonical audit entries on a separate compliance host. Includes migration hooks that preserve existing audit buckets and translate prior envelope formats to the compact form.

Design notes: - Installer KMS routing uses a declarative manifest field: privateInstaller.kms.zoneBindings which maps tenant namespaces to KMS zones. The installer compiles these into a compact L3 routing blob signed by the operator key. Nodes receive the routing blob via the existing secure bootstrap channel. - KMS proxy config supports multi-provider tuples (aws:kms@us-west-2, gcp:kms@europe-west1) and fallbacks; the policy evaluator rejects cross-jurisdiction key usage when the installation policy is strict. - The audit-rehydrate tool accepts a compact envelope store (LZ4+protobuf) and an operator-provided key to expand to full JSON audit rows; expansion can be configured to redact PII using the built-in scrubber rules to match SOC2 requirements. - To avoid changing runtime surface area for hosted customers, all changes are contained to the installer artifacts and the private runtime bootstrap; falling back to existing behavior unless privateInstaller.kms.zoneBindings is set.

Files changed (high level): - installer/cmd/installer/main.go: add preflight and routing compile path. - installer/pkg/kms/router.go: new jurisdictional routing compiler and validators. - installer/cmd/audit-rehydrate/main.go: new tool to expand compact audit envelopes. - installer/config/manifest.schema.yaml: add kms.zoneBindings schema and validation. - charts/private/templates/kms-proxy.yaml: templated KMS proxy sidecar config. - test/e2e/airgap/README.md: new test harness notes and manual steps. - test/e2e/airgap/kms-routing.test: integration test covering manifest->node config flow.

Testing: - Unit tests for router.compile and manifest validation added (router_test.go). - Added an integration e2e that spins up a local air-gapped harness (uses the existing qemu-based appliance image) and verifies node receives signed routing blob and KMS proxy rejects out-of-zone key usage. - audit-rehydrate validated against a corpus of historic envelopes (10k entries) produced by the runtime; results cross-checked with the canonical audit exporter. - CI pipeline updated: installer unit + e2e (airgap) run as optional job flagged by label. All CI checks passed on the final squash.

Migration and operational notes: - Default behavior is opt-in. Existing private installs will not see changes until operators update manifests and run the installer with the new release. - Migration tool included: installer/cmd/migrate-compact-audit which converts legacy envelopes to compact LZ4+protobuf format. - Operators should run the preflight (installer --preflight) prior to upgrade to ensure KMS keys satisfy residency constraints. - Rollout plan: staged rollout to customers on Dedicated->Private track; early access for regulated customers was performed and feedback incorporated.

Security review and approvals: - Threat model: addition of signed routing blob limits attack surface because nodes only accept KMS routing config signed by operator keys; added signature verification unit tests. - RBAC impact: installer now emits placement-time annotations that the runtime's RBAC v2 policy compiler consumes. We updated the compiler docs to include how zoneBindings map to derived roles. - Reviewed by Security: Diego Martinez, Compliance: Liang Wu; changes required to add signature revocation list in case operator keys are rotated — implemented as a revocation file consumed by the bootstrap.

Open items / follow-ups: - Add telemetry to Redwood Console to surface per-tenant KMS-zone enforcement failures (tracked ENG-2211). - Consider adding an offline audit-verify mode that checks integrity of compact envelopes without full rehydration. - UX work to expose preflight failures with clearer remediation suggestions in the installer logs.

Related work: Linear ENG-2148 (jurisdictional KMS routing), SEC-77 (audit replay for air-gapped installs), SUP-2119 (customer ask: EU-only CMK enforcement).
